title: Find the request a reversal cancels

blocks.text: You are on the issuer's side now. `Journal` records every request the issuer has processed, as it arrived from the acquirers' links. When a reversal comes in, `onReversal` acknowledges it and marks the request it cancels as reversed, so the money can go back.

Finish `originalOf(reversal)` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/Journal.java`. When you're done, a reversal cancels exactly the request it is about, wherever and whenever that request came from, and cancels nothing when the issuer never saw that request. About ten lines.
The tests use several acquirers' requests, some of them days apart.

cases.says: a reversal is acknowledged and cancels the one recorded request its field 90 names, not the others
a reversal of a request the issuer never saw is acknowledged and cancels nothing
two requests with the same STAN on different days are different requests; field 90's date and time tell them apart
field 90 carries the institution IDs zero-filled to eleven digits, and eleven zeros for an absent one
a repeated reversal (0421) cancels the original like the first attempt would have

origin.section: 4.4. A Request Without an Answer Is Reversed, Never Sent Again

concepts: A reversal is a new message with its own STAN that names the original in field 90: its MTI, STAN, field 7 and the institution IDs zero-filled to eleven digits.
